items.stem: A call option has a strike of 50 while the stock trades at 57. The call's premium is 9. What is its intrinsic and time value?

options.rationale: Correct: intrinsic value is 57 - 50 = 7, and the remaining 2 of the 9 premium is time value.
Only 7 of the premium is intrinsic; the rest is time value.
Intrinsic value equals how far in-the-money the option is, which is 7.
The call is in-the-money, so intrinsic value is not zero.

items.explanation: Correct: intrinsic value is 57 - 50 = 7, and the remaining 2 of the 9 premium is time value.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about an option's time value are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Time value tends to decay as expiration approaches, all else equal
options.rationale: Correct: theta decay accelerates toward expiration.

options.text: Higher implied volatility generally raises time value
options.rationale: Correct: more expected movement makes the option's optionality more valuable.

options.text: Time value is always equal to the strike price
options.rationale: Time value is a component of the premium, unrelated to the strike level directly.

options.text: Time value cannot change once the option is bought
options.rationale: Time value changes continuously with time and volatility.

items.explanation: Correct: theta decay accelerates toward expiration.

items.stem: A trader sells a covered call against 100 shares they own. What is the main trade-off?

options.text: Premium income now in exchange for capping the upside above the strike
options.rationale: Correct: the covered call earns premium but limits gains if the stock rises past the strike.

options.text: Unlimited additional upside with no obligation
options.rationale: The written call caps upside; it does not add unlimited gains.

options.text: Elimination of all downside risk on the shares
options.rationale: The premium cushions slightly but does not remove downside risk.

options.text: A guarantee the shares will not be called away
options.rationale: The shares can be assigned away if the call is in-the-money.

items.explanation: Correct: the covered call earns premium but limits gains if the stock rises past the strike.
